text:
elaine: Heads-up — after yesterday's continuous-batching heuristic flip we started seeing p95/p99 latency spikes for small requests. Alerting kicked in ~03:10 UTC. Notable drop in throughput too. Anyone looking?
sam: seeing the same in the dashboards. p95 doubled for the <128-token bucket. qps down ~12%. Link: https://grafana.redwood/rt/boards/continuous-batch
perf-bot: ALERT: runtime/latency/p99 > 900ms for bucket=small-reqs for 20m (rule: runtime_p99_small > 800). Triggered at 2026-03-17T03:12:08Z
viv: quick snapshot from profiler on a canary node (3:15 UTC):
```
- avg batch size: 1.7 -> 3.0 after heuristic change
- kernel chosen: matmul_small_batch_fallback (scalar-path) ~ 48% -> 76%
- kv cache hit rate: 94% -> 92% (small dip)
- tail latency correlation: kernel_switch events spike at same timestamps
```
sam: interesting — heuristic is merging lots of small requests into 3-sized batches which pushes shape into a path that chooses the fallback kernel. That kernel has worse per-token latency for short sequences.
elaine: can you paste the kernel decision log? I want to see why routing went to fallback.
sam:
```
[03:14:02] req_id=... batch_size=3 seq_len=48 shape=(3,48) kernel_candidate_scores={fast_matmul: 0.32, small_batch_fallback: 0.68}
[03:14:02] selected_kernel=small_batch_fallback reason="cost_estimate lower latency at predicted throughput"
```
viv: the cost model was re-tuned with a different token-budget target yesterday (target tokens-per-batch increased). That can bias toward forming slightly bigger batches even when kernel affinity prefers single-run fast kernel. I suspect the cost estimator weight for kernel-switch penalty is too low now.
ops-lead: we got a few rollback requests from a support signal. Plan?
elaine: immediate mitigation: revert token-budget target change for the canary cohort and re-run for 30m, then promote; if that fails, revert globally. Can someone run a canary revert?
sam: running patch to revert token_budget_target for canary pool now.
perf-bot: DEPLOY: config/runtime/continuous-batcher token_budget_target revert applied to pool=canary at 2026-03-17T03:22:11Z by sam
viv: fyi ran a quick bpftrace to catch kernel selection hot paths — here's the probe snippet I used:
```
bpftrace -e 'kprobe:kernel_select { @[comm, cpu] = count(); }' -c 'stress-run'
```
and a small post-merge flamegraph shows hotspot in kernel_dispatch::prepare_shaped_weights for those shapes.
elaine: after revert, can we get a 15-minute rolling comparison p50/p95/p99 and avg batch size? Also check KV cache evictions — small change but might have ripple effects.
sam: metrics after canary revert (03:40 UTC window):
```
- p50: 24ms (unchanged)
- p95: 430ms -> 260ms (back to baseline-ish)
- p99: 2100ms -> 540ms
- qps: -12% -> -3% vs pre-deploy
- avg batch size: 3.0 -> 1.8
- kernel fallback rate: 76% -> 34%
```
viv: kernel flip clearly correlated with p99. There's also a small bump in KV cache churn during the spike windows; suspect more prefix mismatches when batches change composition. We should instrument per-request KV key reuse and prefix-similarity.
ops-lead: good rollback. Next steps: 1) revert token_budget_target change for prod until we tune kernel-penalty weight, 2) add telemetry: kernel_choice, cost_score_breakdown, kv_prefix_idx, 3) run a controlled experiment sweeping target values and measuring kernel-affinity and latencies.
elaine: agree. Assigning follow-ups: sam -> prod revert and rollout plan; viv -> add tracepoints for kv prefix reuse and kernel decision scoring; sam+viv -> design sweep experiment. We'll also add an alert refinement to trigger earlier when kernel_fallback_rate for small-batches > 50%.
viv: I'll post the gists with the bpftrace and flamegraph artifacts in #eng-runtime after lunch.
elaine: thanks. One note — let's add a guard in the cost model: if switching kernel increases predicted p95 beyond threshold for bucket=small, prefer current kernel until enough sample evidence. That should reduce oscillation.
sam: noted. I'll file a small RFC and a perf ticket with the data.
perf-bot: TICKET CREATED: RT-4732 "Continuous-batcher: kernel-penalty tuning & kernel-choice telemetry" assigned to sam, viv
ops-lead: marking incident as mitigated after canary revert. Closing on our end but keep thread open for the sweep results. :white_check_mark:
